title: Mapping how LLMs debate societal issues when shadowing human personality traits, sociodemographics and social media behavior

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM-generated discourse by conditioning prompts on synthetic personas with varying attributes such as age, education, occupation, marital status, and migration status, and analyzing the outputs using Textual Forma Mentis Networks (TFMNs).

Analyzing model responses to topics like 'the gender gap in science' and 'STEM stereotypes' by injecting varying biological sex and gender identity attributes into persona-conditioned prompts and measuring semantic and affective differences.
Injecting different sexual orientations into the persona prompt profiles and mapping changes in the models' argumentative logic and framing on sensitive societal issues.
Embedding specific religious beliefs into the generated human personas to systematically observe how faith attributes influence the LLMs' positioning and generated reasoning.

Evaluating how injected psychological traits and OCEAN (Big Five) personality scores influence the models' communication style, epistemic certainty, and emotional tone using semantic network representations.
